whatItFakes: A holder whose party no source gives (six vacant seats with no Ballotpedia vacancy row and the Virgin Islands boards of education and of elections) sits in the party that carried the state in 2024, marked as an estimate.
why: The offices research records each statewide office's term and vacancy rule but not its holder's party, and the legislative roster has no row for a few seats.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Each statewide executive's real party from a public roster (Ballotpedia's partisan composition of state executive offices, or each state's own election results). Oct 23, 2026 (research-gov-sourced-parameters): unrecordedParty in src/core2/modules/officials.ts now reads data/research/offices/unrecorded-holder-parties-2026.json first: the five territory governors (National Governors Association), the American Samoa and Northern Marianas lieutenant governors and attorney general (Wikipedia), ten offices elected without party labels, whose holders sit with no party (Wikipedia, Ballotpedia), the Guam, Virgin Islands, Northern Marianas and American Samoa legislatures (Wikipedia party counts, assigned to their at-large seats in order), and 42 state legislative seats the Open States roster leaves vacant (Ballotpedia's 2025 and 2026 vacancy tables: the departing member's party). whatItFakes: An official whose constituency does not hold the played area (another state's legislators and executives, the House members of the town's state's other districts and of every other state, other states' senators, and the President) weighs their district, their state and the press by their voters' lean alone, with no term for what those voters' lives, faith, degree and news add beyond their leans.
why: The views engine keeps opinion (src/core2/modules/views.ts, keepOpinions) only over the played area's people, full and counted; applying that town's mean to every district in the country would make one town speak for all 56 places.
replacement: Outside places' own opinion: each state's and district's people (the coarse places of the electorate, src/core2/electorate-places.ts) keep their own mean stance by the same rule (groupStance) from their own counted profiles, and an official reads the one their constituency holds.
